result: In real training, curvature grows with the gradient: ‖∇²f‖ ≤ L0 + L1‖∇f‖ ((L0, L1)-smoothness). Under it, fixed-step GD must slow down by a factor tied to the largest gradient it may see, while clipped GD converges at a rate independent of it, so clipping can be arbitrarily faster.
result_plain: Curvature grows with gradient norm; clipped GD's rate doesn't depend on the initial gradient, fixed-step GD's does.
